subject: Trouble adjusting x-scale appropriately- too much white space

messages.author: d6fe5a378b8b1ead
messages.subject: Trouble adjusting x-scale appropriately- too much white space
parts:
I am trying to plot some reactions norms.  The trouble I am having is that I would like for the points/error bars to be closer to the edges of the x-scales.  They are very centered, which makes it difficult to make out the differences between the slopes of the lines.  I want for everything to be on the same y-axis, I would merely like for the 21°C and 31°C points to be further apart from each other within a facet.  I have tried making Temp a factor and a number, but neither approach has fixed the problem.  Below is the code I have used and a sample data set is attached.


opTimeData = read.csv("opTime.csv")

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(opTimeData, aes(x = Temp, y = opTime, colour = Population))+

geom_point(size = 2)+

geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = opTime - ci, ymax = opTime + ci), colour = "black", width = 0.1)+

geom_line(aes(group = paste(Population, Sex)))+

labs(x = "Temperature", y = "Oviposition to pupation time in hours", colour = "Population source location", title = "Immature Development")+

facet_wrap(~ Year + Sex, nrow = 2)+

theme_bw()+

theme(panel.grid = element_blank())+

scale_x_discrete(limits=c("Cool","Hot"), labels = c("21°C","31°C"))+

theme(legend.justification=c(0,1), legend.position="bottom")

add expand=c(0.1,0) to the scale_x_discrete call. You can experiment
with different values; the default seems to be equivalent to c(0.5,0).
Setting it to c(0,0) will bump it directly against the edges, which is
probably too close for aesthetic considerations.

From the documentation:

expand: a numeric vector of length two giving multiplicative and
additive expansion constants. These constants ensure that the data is
placed some distance away from the axes.
